$comment: CONSTITUTIVE DATA — the single home for the Guild's own vocabulary.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. Four constants were shared between
scripts/bmad_drift_check.py and docs/dashboard/generate.py. Two were
IMPORTED (stations, guild_dreams) after a hand-mirrored copy of
guild_dreams drifted on 2026-07-28 and the board warned on a Dream the
Charter explicitly permits. The other two (dream_statuses, dream_types)
were still RE-DECLARED in both files -- identical by luck, not by
construction, and labelled 'Mirrored in ...' as though that were the
design rather than the defect. Doctor Story 6-8 consolidates all four.
WHY HERE, AND NOT IN EITHER CONSUMER. `stations` is the eight Smiths of
docs/dreams/pyforge-charter.md §§1-8 and `guild_dreams` is the Charter
itself: this is constitutive data, not detector or board data, so it
belongs beside the governance kernel rather than inside a tool that
happens to read it. Practically, it also has to be reachable from BOTH
the local-recipes environment (which runs generate.py and cannot import
pyforge.doctor) and from Doctor's own package -- every Doctor source is
repo-rooted via its `target: Path`, so a repo-relative JSON file is
readable from both with no import, no sys.path insert, and no packaging
concern. A new scripts/*.py module would have been ungoverned and would
have needed retiring again by Story 6-9.
STDLIB JSON ON PURPOSE: no YAML dependency, so the leanest environment
can read it.
CHANGING THIS FILE IS A GOVERNANCE ACT. `stations` is the Guild's
membership and `guild_dreams` is the list of Dreams allowed to name no
station. Adding to either is a Charter §5 decision, not a config tweak.
$comment_guild_dreams: The Dreams that may name no station. `guild` is NOT a ninth station.
`pyforge-charter`: the one Dream that CONSTITUTES the stations.
2026-08-08: closed at one. `pyforge-genesis` was absorbed into the
Charter (Dream § Satellite: The Seed; Spec CAP-5..CAP-8) once its
project had dissolved and its installer half had moved to the Marshal --
two names for one record.
2026-09-14: re-opened by Charter amendment for exactly one further
shape -- a gate that judges all eight Smiths, which no Smith can own
without grading itself on one row (Charter Section 5, the doctrine
applied to itself). `coverage-gate-independence` is that gate. The test
is structural: cross-cutting, shared or unowned does NOT qualify; the
artifact must judge every Smith. Its mechanism stories stay a Smith's
(Doctor's) under the outcome/mechanism rule.
2026-09-16: the same shape a second time. `one-chain-per-station` amends
the Lexicon's reading of Dream-first (Dream-append-first) and mints
`chain-sprawl-check`, a gate over every Smith's planning tree -- no Smith
can own a rule that grades its own Dream and Spec count (steward alone
carries 22 open Dreams). Operator-ruled 2026-09-16 (six rulings in the
Spec memlog). Mechanism stories stay Doctor's; the per-station fold
stories stay each Smith's. Whether the Lexicon amendment also needs the
Section 5 ritual is the Spec's third open question.
$comment_fold_exemptions: The CLOSED list of reasons a NEW docs/dreams/*.md file or specs/spec-*/ folder may exist
outside a station's one chain (spec-one-chain-per-station CAP-1, operator 2026-09-16).
Dream-APPEND-first: new work is a dated section of the station Dream + a CAP on the station
Spec + a Story -- never a new file. chain-sprawl-check (doctor 25.1) reads THIS list and
nothing else (vocabulary-one-name-one-job CAP-2: one declared source). Adding a value here
is a governance act; the four are: different-owner (the work has a different accountable
Smith), different-lifecycle (it ends when the station does not), cross-station-seam (a
shared package every station imports -- pyforge-core, the testing kit), governance (a
Lexicon amendment cannot be a section of a station Dream).
$comment_dream_statuses: The Dream lifecycle -- each state names the ACT THAT COMPLETED. There is
deliberately no `building` state: status declares what EXISTS (stable,
honestly hand-declarable) and the board DERIVES what is happening from
live build lines. A `building` status was considered and rejected -- it
would go stale the moment a line pauses or finishes, which is exactly how
pyforge-warden came to read `in-spec` while shipped 31/31, and deckcraft
`dreamt` while holding a deck AND a Spec (both found + fixed 2026-07-25).
$comment_dream_types: `practice` marks a perpetual concern -- tended, never finished. They sit
OUTSIDE the lifecycle: excluded from backlog (nobody can close them) and
$comment_spec_statuses: The Spec lifecycle -- all eight live values, one definition each. Before
this declaration (steward Story 59.1), only `extension-point` carried a
prose definition (docs/dreams/README.md); the other seven existed only
as hardcoded sets split across pyforge.doctor.sources.board
(OPEN_SPEC_STATUSES / DELIVERED_SPEC_STATUSES, covering draft / ready /
in-progress / shipped) and pyforge.doctor.sources.one_chain
(_CLOSED_SPEC_STATUSES, covering archived / absorbed / superseded).
docs/governance/spec-one-chain-per-station/CHAIN-STANDARD.md §4 already
listed all eight values in a summary table (added 2026-09-17), but with
no per-value definition and not machine-readable -- that gap, not the
bare enumeration, is this declaration's actual delta.
`draft`: the contract's open questions are unanswered; nothing downstream
can bind to it yet.
`ready`: the contract binds, forever -- CAPs carry `(Met <date>)` as they
land.
`in-progress`: GRANDFATHERED -- see spec_statuses_grandfathered below.
Never written to a new Spec; existing files stay open until next edited.
`shipped`: every CAP delivered. Spec-terminal -- see spec_statuses_terminal
below -- and a Spec-only fact, distinct from story `done` and Dream
`realized` (the full cross-walk lives in the Charter's Lexicon, not here).
`archived`: abandoned outright, not delivered.
`absorbed`: folded into another chain; its CAPs live in the absorbing
chain's own epic.
`superseded`: replaced by a later Spec; abandoned, not delivered.
`extension-point`: a recognised parked-Spec state -- the chain exists and
the contract is deliberately left open, a seam a later effort extends. It
does NOT satisfy a Dream's `specified` (docs/dreams/README.md) -- the
Spec-side sibling of a Dream's `dreamt`.
THE THREE ENDED ACTS. `archived`, `absorbed`, and `superseded` all mean
the Spec stopped without shipping, but they answer different questions --
abandoned outright, folded into a sibling chain, or replaced by a
successor -- so they stay three distinct values and are never collapsed
into one (spec_statuses_ended_acts).
SHIPPED IS TERMINAL, NOT AN ENDED ACT. `shipped` is grouped as
Spec-terminal (spec_statuses_terminal = the three ended acts plus
`shipped`) precisely because it is NOT one of the three ended acts -- it
is the one terminal value that delivered rather than ended.
GRANDFATHERED. `in-progress` is the sole grandfathered value
(spec_statuses_grandfathered): no new Spec may be minted at it, and
existing Specs stay open until next edited. See
docs/governance/spec-one-chain-per-station/CHAIN-STANDARD.md §4 for what
finally retires it.
RECOMMENDED, NOT REQUIRED. This enum is recommended, not required. A
Spec carrying an unregistered status value must be preserved exactly as
written and must produce a warning -- it must never be silently reset to
a value in this list.
$comment_spec_statuses_ready_or_beyond: Backs docs/dreams/README.md:71's rule: a Dream at `specified` needs a covering
own CAP-1-vocabulary subset -- five Story/ledger/Dream words outside CAP-1's enum
stay literal in that module and are never sourced from here).
Spec does not satisfy the Dream's contract. `absorbed` IS included -- its CAPs
live on in the absorbing chain, so the contract is still covered, just elsewhere.
This is a derived grouping of already-declared spec_statuses values (steward
Story 59.2), the same kind of addition as spec_statuses_terminal/_ended_acts/
_grandfathered above -- not a Charter Section 5 act (that clause guards
`stations`/`guild_dreams` specifically, per this file's own top comment).
$comment_session_denials: The CLOSED list of what `.claude/hooks/pre-shell.py` denies -- the Guild
session guardrails, enforced rather than merely asserted in AGENTS.md/
CLAUDE.md prose (steward Story 63.3, spec-pyforge-steward CAP-5). ONE
script serves both harnesses (Claude Code's `PreToolUse` on `Bash` and on
warn -- Cursor has no before-edit deny). Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot CLI
and Devin have no verified deny surface for this hook; the ten rules stay
instruction-only there, as written in AGENTS.md.
Each entry's `id` MUST have exactly one matching callable in the script's
own `MATCHERS` dict, in both directions -- `load_denial_rules()` raises
(fail loud, never a silent skip) on any drift between the two, at every
invocation. `reason` is the one-line message shown to the agent, naming
the sanctioned form; for the two rules with more than one trigger shape
keyed by sub-case rather than a single string.
CHANGING THIS LIST IS A GOVERNANCE ACT, same as `stations`/`guild_dreams`
above: adding, removing or reshaping a denial is a deliberate decision,
never a drive-by code edit to pre-shell.py alone. The hook never denies

session_denials.trigger: pixi run -e local-recipes <task>, where <task> is in the guild-tasks set read live from pixi.toml's [feature.guild-tasks.tasks] -- never a copy
session_denials.reason: '{task}' is a Guild task -- rerun as `pixi run -e pyforge-guild {task}`; -e local-recipes only carries it for back-compat.

session_denials.trigger: pip install / uv pip install / conda install / npx <x> other than npx skills add
session_denials.reason: Dependencies are pinned in pixi.toml + pixi.lock, not installed ad hoc -- add it to pixi.toml in a PR, or use `npx skills add` for a skill install.
a dependency is a pixi.toml change in a PR, not a live `pixi add`/`pixi update` -- edit pixi.toml, run `pixi lock`, and open a PR (regenerate environment.yaml too).

session_denials.trigger: scripts/bmad-switch run from a worktree, or with BMAD_ACTIVE_PROJECT already set
session_denials.reason: Never run scripts/bmad-switch from a worktree or parallel agent -- it mutates shared per-working-tree state; set BMAD_ACTIVE_PROJECT=<slug> and address _bmad-output/projects/<slug>/ by its physical path instead.

session_denials.trigger: git commit on main, in the primary checkout, or with a Co-Authored-By / AI-attribution line

reason.checkout: Never commit on main or in the primary checkout -- branch from origin/main into a worktree (`pyforge steward workspace start <slug>`) and commit there.
reason.attribution: Commit messages carry no Co-Authored-By line and no AI attribution -- the commit-msg hook already refuses these (AGENTS.md Policy); drop the line.

session_denials.reason: Merge with `gh pr merge --merge`, never `--squash` -- squash is disabled in repository settings and a squash subject orphans landing-evidence detection.
Create with `gh pr create --repo rxm7706/local-recipes` -- omitting --repo can target the wrong repository.

session_denials.trigger: uv run with cwd != the repo (or worktree) root
session_denials.reason: Run `uv run` from the repo root -- from a subdirectory it creates a stray .venv there; cd to the repo/worktree root first.
Stamp scoped: `python scripts/spec_surface_check.py --write-baseline --spec <project>/<spec>` -- a bare --write-baseline accepts every other Spec's pending drift as correct.

session_denials.trigger: a direct write to SPEC.md, sprint-status-ledger.yaml, or a tracked path under implementation-artifacts/

reason.spec_md: Never hand-edit a SPEC.md -- append to its .memlog.md with `uv run _bmad/scripts/memlog.py` and re-derive with bmad-spec.
reason.ledger: Never hand-edit sprint-status-ledger.yaml (generated) -- write the Tier-3 feed, then `pixi run -e pyforge-guild sprint-ledger-sync -- --project <station>`.
reason.implementation_artifacts: Never track anything under implementation-artifacts/ -- it is Tier 3 and gitignored; this path is already tracked, which is the bug to fix, not to perpetuate by editing it further.
